questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
questions.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-2,4)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,-2,4⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =⟨1,-2,4⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26 \\ 3y-5z & =-26 \\ 3y-5z+26 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

${\begin{aligned}x=-2+t \\ y=1+4t \\ z=5\end{aligned}.$

First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,-4,1⟩.$  From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨1,4,0⟩.$  So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨1,4,0⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =⟨2,-4,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =-14\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =-14 \\ x+4y & =-14 \\ x+4y+14 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $x-y+4z+16=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨1,-1,4⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y+4z+16 & =0 \\ z & =-\frac{1}{4}x+\frac{1}{4}y-4.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=-4.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,-4)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,-4⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-4⟩)\cdot ⟨1,-1,4⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,-1,1)$, $P(2,0,3)$ and $Q(1,1,0).$
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,-1,1⟩,\,p=⟨2,0,3⟩,$ and $q=⟨1,1,0⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨2,0,3⟩-⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,2⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩-⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,2,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-5i+j+2k \\  & =⟨-5,1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =⟨2,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =-4 \\ -5x+y+2z & =-4 \\ -5x+y+2z+4 & =0 \\ 5x-y-2z-4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,0,3)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=⟨5,2,1⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨0,3,3⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,0,3⟩.$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =3i-15j+15k \\  & =⟨3,-15,15⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ & =⟨1,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ & =48\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ & =48 \\ 3x-15y+15z & =48 \\ 3x-15y+15z-48 & =0 \\ x-5y+5z-16 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-4i+2j+6k \\  & =⟨-4,2,6⟩\end{aligned}

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =⟨3,-1,4⟩\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =10 \\ -4x+2y+6z & =10 \\ -4x+2y+6z-10 & =0 \\ 4x-2y-6z+10 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,1,-1)$, $P(3,4,2)$ and $Q(-1,2,0).$

$\,y\,-\,z\,-$
{{field-1}}
$=0$
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,1,-1⟩,\,p=⟨3,4,2⟩,$ and $q=⟨-1,2,0⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨3,4,2⟩-⟨1,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,3,3⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨-1,2,0⟩-⟨1,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 3 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =0i-8j+8k \\  & =⟨0,-8,8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,-8,8⟩ & =⟨3,4,2⟩\cdot ⟨0,-8,8⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,-8,8⟩ & =-16\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,-8,8⟩ & =-16 \\ -8y+8z & =-16 \\ -8y+8z+16 & =0 \\ y-z-2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
canonical_examples.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(9,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $\mathbf{n}=3\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}+7\mathbf{k}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle 9,-2,3 \rangle$ and the normal vector of the plane is $\mathbf{n}=\langle 3,-4,7 \rangle.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =⟨9,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =56.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =56 \\ 3x-4y+7z & =56 \\ 3x-4y+7z-56 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Line
canonical_examples.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-1,4,8)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$\dfrac{x+3}{-5}=\dfrac{y-1}{3}=\dfrac{z+2}{2}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle -1,4,8 \rangle.$ From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $\langle -5,3,2 \rangle.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
\mathbf{n}=\langle -5,3,2 \rangle.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =⟨-1,4,8⟩\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =33\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =33 \\ -5x+3y+2z & =33 \\ -5x+3y+2z-33 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Plane Given Its Cartesian Equation
canonical_examples.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $2x-y+z+13=0$ of the plane $\Pi,$ find an equation of $\Pi$ in the form $(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{p})\cdot\mathbf{n}=0.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, from the coefficients in equation of the plane, we get that the normal vector of $\Pi$ is $\mathbf{n}=\langle 2,-1,1 \rangle.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $\Pi$ for $z\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y+z+13 & =0 \\ z & =-2x+y-13\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0,$ we get $z=-13.$ So, the point $P(0,0,-13)$ lies on $\Pi.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle 0,0,-13 \rangle.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-13⟩)\cdot ⟨2,-1,1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Vectors
canonical_examples.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-3,2,-6)$ and is parallel to the vectors $\mathbf{v_1}=\langle -3, 5, 2 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{v_2}=\langle 1, 3, -2 \rangle.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle -3,2,-6 \rangle.$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $\mathbf{v_1}$ and $\mathbf{v_2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 5 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-16i-4j-14k \\  & =⟨-16,-4,-14⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =⟨-3,2,-6⟩\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =124\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =124 \\ -16x-4y-14z & =124 \\ -16x-4y-14z-124 & =0 \\ 8x+2y+7z+62 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
